agent_note: Dual-timeline but single narrating stance: a third-person past frame following Maggie in the present day (q05715, q05731, q05744, q05748, q05750) and an embedded first-person past strand about her sixteen-year-old self (q05711, q05712, q05728, q05737, q05745). q05727 shows the seam - Maggie says 'In 1995, when I was sixteen years old, I began to lead a secret life' inside past-tense frame narration. Both strands are retrospective, so the dual structure does not make the book tense-dual. 27 event quotes, 27 past / 0 present - no present-tense event narration anywhere in the sample. The 13 gnomic quotes are all present-tense aphorism, the classic Goodreads quotability bias; a two-bucket filter would have called this book 33% present on quotes like 'teaching is impossible unless a student wants to learn.' Five past-tense generalizations (q05706, q05716, q05721, q05732, and the reasoning in q05715) were counted as event/past per the gnomic-is-present-only rule; q05708 and q05721 are the same claim in the two tenses and split across the two buckets accordingly. Four unmarked speech quotes (q05726, q05729, q05743, q05746) were called dialogue on content rather than quotation marks - all four are present-tense, so reading them as narration would have manufactured the book's only present-tense evidence. Nothing lands near a threshold: no single quote flips this book, and it is nowhere near the flagged 70-85% present band.
